findings.title: remove_member bypasses GroupUser callbacks and 404s for non-members
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` on a `has_many :through` association deletes the join rows with `delete_all`, so no `GroupUser` callbacks run. Consequences: the cached `groups.user_count` column is never decremented (the admin UI shows a stale member count and pagination computed from it), and other per-membership side effects (clearing `primary_group`, notification-level/title cleanup) are skipped. Note the opposite path (`add_members` → `group.add(user)`) does create the join record through the model, so counts drift only on removal. Additionally, `CollectionProxy#delete` with an integer id calls `find` internally, so deleting a user that is not a member raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` (rendered as 404) instead of a graceful response. Use the model API (`group.remove(user)` / destroy the `GroupUser` record) instead.

findings.title: Unvalidated limit/offset on public members endpoint
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to `.limit()/.offset()` with no clamping. An anonymous caller can request `?limit=1000000` and force the server to load and serialize the whole membership of a large group (cheap DoS), and `?limit=-1` or `?offset=-1` produces a negative LIMIT/OFFSET which PostgreSQL rejects, turning into a 500 error. Clamp limit to a sane maximum (e.g. 50..100) and floor offset at 0.

findings.title: Breaking response-shape change for GET /groups/:name/members
findings.body: The endpoint previously returned a bare JSON array of serialized users (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`); it now returns `{members: [...], meta: {...}}`. Any external API consumer, plugin or cached front-end asset that expects the array form will break with no versioning or deprecation path. If the change is intentional it should at least be called out in the PR/release notes and covered by a spec (none exists for this endpoint in this PR).

findings.title: Public group member list is silently truncated to 50 with no pagination UI
findings.body: Previously non-automatic groups returned all members (only automatic groups were limited, default 200). Now every request is limited to 50 by default, but the public group page template (`discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`) renders `members` with no next/previous controls, so a group with more than 50 members shows only the first 50 and users have no way to see the rest. Either add pagination to the public template or keep returning the full list there.

findings.title: totalPages off-by-one produces an extra empty page
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed in admin-group.js.es6 as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which over-counts whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100 members / 50 per page → 3 pages instead of 2). Combined with `next`, which clamps `offset` to `user_count` (`Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), the admin can page to an offset equal to the total and see an empty member list labelled e.g. "3/3". Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` and advance offset in whole pages.

findings.title: update unconditionally resets `visible` when the param is absent
findings.body: `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` runs on every update, so any PUT to /admin/groups/:id that omits `visible` (now a flat-param API, so partial updates are natural, e.g. sending only `alias_level`) silently makes the group invisible. Only assign when the parameter is present (`group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" if params.key?(:visible)`).

findings.title: create silently drops alias_level
findings.body: The client's `asJSON()` (discourse/models/group.js) sends `name`, `alias_level` and `visible` for both create and update, but `create` only reads `name` and `visible`. A group created with a non-default alias level in the admin UI is persisted with the default alias level, and the admin gets no indication the setting was ignored. Assign `alias_level` here as `update` does.

findings.title: add_members raises on array usernames param and silently ignores unknown users
findings.body: `usernames.split(",")` assumes a String; if a client posts `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` (a natural form for this parameter) `params.require(:usernames)` yields an Array and `split` raises NoMethodError → 500. Also, usernames that don't resolve to a user are skipped without any report, so the admin sees "success" while some members were not added. Accept both forms (`Array(usernames).flat_map { |u| u.split(",") }`) and return the list of names that could not be added.

findings.title: addMembers/removeMember swallow errors and resolve before the reload completes
findings.body: Both methods call `self.findMembers()` inside `then` without returning its promise, so callers' `then` fires before the member list is refreshed, and neither has a rejection handler. If the server responds 422 (e.g. automatic group) or 404, the admin UI shows nothing at all — the click appears to do nothing. Return the inner promise and surface failures (e.g. bootbox.alert with the server error), as `save`/`create` do.

findings.title: Member add/remove specs use the wrong verb and don't assert counter integrity
findings.body: `xhr :put, :remove_member` exercises the action with PUT even though the only route to `remove_member` is DELETE, so a verb/route mismatch would not be caught. More importantly, no spec asserts that removing a member updates `group.user_count` (the current implementation using `group.users.delete` leaves it stale), that removing a non-member behaves gracefully, or that `add_members` ignores unknown usernames (a case that had explicit coverage before this PR and was deleted). There is also no spec at all for the reshaped `GET /groups/:name/members` response (`members` + `meta`) or its limit/offset handling.
